title: Jim Cramer has a strong verdict on Anthropic CEO message
excerpt: Jim Cramer had a one-word description for what drove the recent AI selloff.
content_html:
Hillary Remy

Wed, September 16, 2026 at 6:47 PM PDT 5 min read

Wall Street always finds something new to panic about, and this time it found the reason wrapped in language usually reserved for existential risk. A widely read essay warning that artificial intelligence needs to slow down rattled traders just as several of the market's biggest winners depend on that same technology continuing to accelerate at full speed.

Jim Cramer decided the panic had gone far enough. Rather than simply reacting to the headline, he broke down why he thinks the warning deserves skepticism and laid out exactly how investors should respond instead of selling on fear.

Cramer's objection to the Anthropic CEO slowdown manifesto

Cramer did not mince words about the essay driving the panic. He called the posting "self-evident and extremely self-serving," according to CNBC, pointing out that a self-imposed slowdown in AI data center spending would land hardest on the stocks most tied to that buildout, starting with Nvidia.

His skepticism toward the messenger is not new. Cramer has previously noted that Amodei has made dramatic public claims before that did not hold up over time, CNBC reported.

Cramer placed the current scare alongside a familiar pattern. He referenced JPMorgan chief executive Jamie Dimon's "cockroach theory" comment about credit risk, noting that a warning many investors took as a sign of deeper trouble ultimately did not spread nearly as far as feared. A pattern he sees repeating with the AI slowdown narrative.

To explain the apparent contradiction of a CEO warning against his own product, Cramer pointed to David Sacks, the White House AI and crypto czar, who called the framing what it likely is. Sacks wrote on X that AI labs demanding their preferred regulatory framework as the price of pacing development "will look like blackmail of the public and the political system."

The Anthropic CEO essay causing the uproar

The essay behind the uproar came from Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, who published a roughly 3,800-word piece titled "We Must Pace the Frontier" on September 12, arguing the industry should deliberately slow how fast it improves model capabilities. Sam Altman at OpenAI and Elon Musk at xAI both signaled support within hours, according to CNBC.

Amodei's manifesto did not come out of nowhere. He has spent much of the past year making similarly dramatic claims in public, previously telling Axios that AI could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs within five years and push unemployment as high as 10% to 20%, a warning TheStreet had covered.
